title: openai-compat: normalize tool_choice semantics and streaming tool events
author: Chen Li
release_notes: Stabilize OpenAI compatibility for function/tool calling: introduce canonical tool_choice handling and emit structured streaming events for tool calls. SDKs should pick up new streaming events; no behaviour change for existing non-streaming clients.
description:
Motivation: the OpenAI-compatible layer had inconsistent behavior around function/tool calling when converting between Redwood internal tool schemas and OpenAI-style 'tools'. In particular: (1) tool_choice was sometimes returned as a flat string, sometimes as an object; (2) streamed responses mixed assistant->tool chunks with no explicit event markers, which made SDK handling for incremental tool outputs brittle; (3) tool messages in some backends used the assistant role instead of an explicit 'tool' event payload. This PR standardizes semantics so downstream SDKs and customers using the OpenAI-compat surface get deterministic, documented events for tool/function calls.

What this change does (high level):
- Adds a canonical mapping layer that converts Redwood tool metadata to an OpenAI 'function' schema and back. This includes explicit type mapping for parameters, required fields and description fields.
- Introduces a normalized 'tool_choice' semantic: the compatibility layer will emit tool_choice as an object with 'name' and optional 'arguments' keys in OpenAI-style responses; for plain text compat responses (legacy) we still keep string shims but log a deprecation warning.
- Streaming: we now emit structured streaming events for tool lifecycle: TOOL_INVOKE, TOOL_STDOUT (chunk), TOOL_FINISH. These are encoded in the OpenAI streaming channel as JSON-prefixed events with event types in the delta payload so SDKs can react to intermediate tool outputs without treating them as assistant tokens. The events are also mirrored to the Redwood internal message bus using existing trace IDs.
- Tool message formatting: tool outputs are wrapped in a tool message envelope with metadata (tool_name, exit_code, meta) so tools that return structured JSON are preserved intact and non-JSON outputs are transmitted as text chunks.
- Backwards compatibility: non-streaming endpoints and previously-recorded function_call objects still produce compatible shapes. The OpenAI compat adapter will attempt to translate legacy responses to the new shape where possible.

Files/areas touched (summary):
- openai_compat/adapter.py - main mapping logic + streaming event serializer
- openai_compat/mapping.py - canonical parameter/schema conversion utilities
- runtime/tool_runner.py - small change to emit lifecycle events and envelope tool outputs
- sdk/openai_compat/stream_parser.ts - updated to parse TOOL_* events and rehydrate function call sequences for TS SDK
- tests/integration/test_tool_streaming.py - new integration tests that simulate long-running tools and chunked output
- docs/openai-compat.md - documentation for the new streaming events and migration notes

Migration notes for integrators:
- Type: minor API surface extension. Streaming clients should update to pick up TOOL_INVOKE/TOOL_STDOUT/TOOL_FINISH events. Non-streaming clients unaffected.
- SDKs: the TypeScript SDK update (small patch) is included in this PR and will be released in the next patch; Python and Go SDKs should follow but will remain compatible.
- Deprecation: legacy string-only tool_choice will be deprecated in 3 months; we emit a warn-level audit log when it is returned.

Testing:
- Added unit tests around the mapping layer (mapping conversion including nested parameter schemas).
- Added integration tests that run a fake tool which emits a JSON object, then text chunks; the streaming parser asserts the order of TOOL_INVOKE -> TOOL_STDOUT* -> TOOL_FINISH and that rehydrated outputs match the original content.
- Ran end-to-end smoke on staging with Redwood Dedicated and the private installer to confirm no regressions in non-OpenAI endpoints.

Checklist:
- [x] mapper implementation + unit tests
- [x] streaming event serializer + parser updates
- [x] TS SDK stream parser patch included
- [x] integration test for chunked tool output
- [x] docs + migration notes

Related: linear/ENG-3241, ENG-3310; support ticket SUP-784 for customer encountering mixed-assistant/tool chunks.

Design note: we chose explicit event types rather than overloading assistant deltas because expanding the token stream with special sentinel tokens was brittle across different downstream SDKs and made partial-detokenization hard. The JSON-prefixed event approach is backwards compatible with existing token streams (they see a short JSON delta) and is easy to parse safely.

If you'd like to test locally: run `pytest tests/integration/test_tool_streaming.py` and run the TS SDK demo in `sdk/openai_compat/demo` with the staging compat endpoint.
